sections.heading: New
items: Keep it now keeps it. Press the button under your finished film and the film lands in your Movies folder, then Finder opens with it selected. Before this, that button opened an export panel with six dropdowns — destination, codec, resolution, timeline format, and two more you had never heard of. If you want those, the Export button in the title bar still has them.

While your film is being written, you can read it. Each empty frame now carries the line of narration for that shot, arriving one at a time as they are written — instead of thirty seconds of blank slots.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The Chinese progress line was backwards. It said "0 of 5 shots are in" with the numbers swapped, which read as "out of 0 shots, 5 have arrived."
Credits had four different names in Chinese. Now it has one.
A film whose name is a long sentence saves correctly. Long non-Latin names were being cut past the filesystem's limit and failing to save at all.
Saving two films with the same name no longer overwrites the first one.

sections.heading: Known limits
items: Requires macOS 26. Earlier systems cannot run it.
Crash reporting is still not connected. If METAG crashes on your Mac we will not know — please tell us.

sections.heading: New
items: Films come alive when you look at them. Hover a poster on the first screen and it starts playing — silent, looping, no click. The same gesture works on your own films.

When your film lands, it plays itself from the top. A quiet bar asks what you want to do: keep it, make another, or edit it yourself. Before this you got eleven clips on three tracks and a line in a side panel.
Sign-in that stalls now says so. If the browser hand-off is slow we stop pretending and offer to open it again — we never claim it failed, because we don't know that.
The first screen is the product now, not a welcome card in front of it.
While a film is being shot, each empty slot holds that shot's line from the storyboard, large enough to read, plus a count of how many have landed.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The sign-in row in the account popover lines up with the rest of the menu.
"No music model" is no longer a red dead end — it is a calm line with a door to Settings.
The export panel no longer gives half the window to an empty queue.
Every gap in the interface now sits on a 4pt grid. Nothing moved much; everything moved a little.
The four sign-in buttons always carry a line explaining them, even when we can't reach the server for the free-credit number.

sections.heading: Known limits
items: Requires macOS 26. Earlier systems cannot run it.
Crash reporting is still not connected. If METAG crashes on your Mac we will not know — please tell us.

sections.heading: New
items: Your film plays the moment it lands. A quiet bar over it asks what you want to do — keep it, make another, or edit it yourself. Before this you got eleven clips on three tracks and a line in a side panel.
Three real films on the first screen. Click one and it plays right there — no sign-up, no wait, no credits.
Your films are a wall of posters. Hover one and it starts playing, so you know which one it is without opening it.
Opened from the disk image, METAG asks once and moves itself into Applications. Running from the image means updates can never install, and the app disappears when you eject.
The installer window shows where to drag it.
While a film is being shot, each empty slot holds that shot's line from the storyboard, large enough to read, and a count of how many have landed.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Buttons that spend money no longer print a price we do not have yet. One of them used to say “Approve 0 Credits” while the quote was still loading.
We no longer claim nothing was charged unless we have confirmed the refund. When we do not know, we say we are checking.
A failed balance check no longer shows a red zero, and a failed price list no longer makes the buy button disappear for the rest of the session.
Re-shoot failures say what actually happened — needs a subscription, hourly limit, shot still busy, wrong account — instead of one sentence for all of them.
Errors from the server no longer reach the screen as raw HTML or a stack trace.

0.1.9 through 0.1.12 were withdrawn the day they shipped: they were signed with a certificate the embedded profile did not list, so macOS killed them at launch. If you have one of those, download this build. Every release is now started once before it ships.

sections.heading: New
items: Fixed shots, re-shoots and takes now report what actually happened, in your language — those screens used to be Chinese only
Out of credits? You can buy them right where you ran out, instead of being sent to Settings first
The draft panel says which step it is on — writing the shot list, choosing a voice, recording the narration — rather than a spinner

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Exports no longer stall on muted audio
Clicking the home screen works again after dismissing What's New
Switching project windows no longer hangs
Compositions reuse source assets instead of rebuilding them
The storyboard no longer sends per-shot seconds the gateway does not accept

sections.heading: Known limits
items: Generation covers video only — image, audio and upscale models are not offered yet
Reference images and reference video are not accepted, which keeps your footage on your machine

sections.heading: New
items: Every user-visible screen now says METAG — the upstream name is gone
Your film library shows what each one cost and how many shots it has

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Rate limits now say whose quota ran out — your own hourly limit reads differently from us being busy
Failures say what to do about them: an expired job, a draft still rendering, a file over the size limit

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixing several flagged shots now undoes as one action — it was one step per shot, so one ⌘Z only put back the last one
A re-shoot no longer reports success when the clip was deleted while it was running
Picking a take is no longer blocked forever if the render process restarts mid-re-shoot

Exported recipes carry the visuals, not the narration text; comparing takes side by side is still web-only

sections.heading: Fix flagged shots in one step
items: Right-click any generated clip → Re-shoot → Fix Flagged Shots. Only shots an automatic check thinks are broken get re-run
The machine judges whether a shot is usable — frozen, flickering, solid colour. Whether it is good stays your call, so nothing is picked on taste
What you already have is kept as a take, and each swap is one undo

File → Import Recipe rebuilds a film from one, so a film moves between this app, the web editor, and a teammate
Rebuilding always uses our own engine — someone else's recipe cannot spend your credits at flagship rates

items: Saving a project no longer races the snapshot it is writing — a save issued mid-edit could previously block or drop the newest change
The open and save panels are pre-warmed at launch, so the first Open no longer stalls for a second
Scrubbing no longer fills the audio cache automatically, which kept the timeline responsive on long projects

Word-level removal is available to the agent panel as a tool, so you can ask for a phrase to be cut by name

sections.heading: First public release
items: Multi-track editing, colour, effects, captions, and export all run on your Mac
AI shot generation goes through the METAG gateway: sign in once, pay per shot, failed jobs are refunded
On-device transcription and captions via Apple SpeechAnalyzer — audio never leaves your Mac, and it is free
Agent panel drives the timeline with your own Anthropic key; the same tools are exposed over local MCP
Interface available in English, Simplified Chinese, and Spanish
